runs.title: CFB Wainwright tragedy: the official word
runs.prompt: Four Canadian Armed Forces members were killed and dozens injured in a fire during a training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta in mid-October 2026. Find out: (1) how many were killed and how many injured in total, (2) what the National Defence / Government of Canada has said officially about the cause and any updates, and (3) whether there is a November 2026 update on the injured personnel. Start with the official Department of National Defence news pages and the CFB Wainwright fire Wikipedia article, and report what you find from public pages.
runs.answer: (1) 4 Canadian Armed Forces members were killed — Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark (3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry) — and 39 were injured in the fire at CFB Wainwright on 17 October 2026 (DND's tallies reconcile: 27 in hospital + 12 released on 22 Oct; 25 + 14 on 4 Nov). (2) Officially, National Defence (22 Oct release) says the Military Police are running an independent investigation to establish the facts and whether any criminal or service offences occurred, and that a separate, independent Board of Inquiry is being convened with terms of reference being developed; DND has not publicly assigned a cause. Wikipedia describes the fire as starting during live-fire training on an artillery range (Exercise APOLLO SHOOTER at Permanent Danger Area 2) and spreading in high winds, with officials stating oil/gas operations were not involved. (3) Yes — a 4 November 2026 DND statement confirms 25 injured members remain hospitalized, 14 have been released, and four hospitalized members were transferred to facilities nearer their homes in British Columbia and Ontario.

runs.title: Stunt: pry Rex Ryan's charges from ESPN
runs.prompt: Former NFL coach Rex Ryan has reportedly been charged after allegedly hitting pedestrians with a car in Nashville. Attempt to retrieve the actual details of the charges and what happened directly from ESPN's NFL page (espn.com), which is known to block automated readers. Document exactly what you can and cannot access, and whether any public plain-GET fetch returns the story. Then note where else the facts might be obtained.
runs.answer: ESPN is fully walled off to plain GETs: https://www.espn.com/, /nfl/, /nfl/news/ and the exact story page /nfl/story/_/id/50453897/rex-ryan-facing-charges-alleged-hit-run all returned HTTP 202 with zero readable text (no headlines, no body), and its JSON feed site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/nfl/news returned HTTP 403. No public plain-GET fetch of ESPN returned the story — the headline and URL only surfaced via a DuckDuckGo snippet. The facts, confirmed by The Guardian and Nashville's WSMV: Ryan turned himself in to Metro Nashville Police on Wed. Nov 11, 2026, on six misdemeanor warrants over a Nov. 4 incident at Fourth Ave. and Broadway, where his pickup turned right at a red light into pedestrians crossing with the walk signal, ran over both people's feet and struck one person's leg (minor injuries); he stopped at a red light, argued with them, then drove off. Charges: two counts each of leaving the scene of an accident, failure to give information/render aid, and failure to obey a traffic control signal; bond $6,000, court date next month. Pedestrians photographed him and the plate, which registered to Ryan. ESPN's own version is syndicated elsewhere: sports.yahoo.
